synopsis:
At Kirin Arts High School, preparations for an overseas showcase are already under way when the disappearance of Song Samdong casts a long shadow over the students. Once a top K-pop star and a figure shaped by the school, Samdong has vanished, leaving behind both unanswered questions and the daunting image of a dream fulfilled, then abruptly lost.

The school now operates under a new educational system built to produce global stars. Achievement, evaluation, and competition take precedence, and the pressure to stand out becomes inseparable from the students' pursuit of the stage. As they train for the showcase, the students of Kirin Arts High School must confront what it means to chase a future in an environment that measures them chiefly by results. Their ambitions propel them forward, yet the demand to become exceptional threatens to leave those who cannot keep pace behind.

Teacher Kang Ohhyeok watches them closely. Having once seen a student collapse while trying too hard to become perfect, he refuses to hurry young people who are still learning how to dream. Samdong's absence makes that lesson more urgent: the students are not merely preparing a performance, but trying to find a way to move toward new dreams without losing themselves to fear, comparison, or the expectations imposed upon them.

As the overseas showcase approaches, the students continue toward the stage together. In the space between Samdong's unresolved disappearance and their own uncertain futures, they must decide whether success alone is the destination, or whether their dreams can retain their meaning even amid competition.

The musical considers the cost of pursuing excellence in a system ruled by performance and results. It ultimately centres on young people protecting their own dreams, learning to endure uncertainty, and finding the courage to keep moving forward together.

synopsis:
Makgeolli stands before the doors of Lolo BAR, listening for the roar that once greeted him as the legendary flare bartender of a decade ago. Still haunted by those cheers and determined to reclaim the thrilling image he remembers, he prepares to open a new bar with grand ambitions. Yet the people around him fail to meet his expectations. Apart from the Manager, who has endured the years beside him through every high and low, Makgeolli finds no one he can truly accept as part of his dream. Disappointed and discouraged, he faces the possibility that the bar he has imagined so vividly may never become the place capable of reviving his former glory.

Then the door of Lolo BAR cracks open and a voice calls, “Hello, I saw the poster.” The unexpected arrival begins to change the atmosphere. A Student with secret cocktail-making skills appears, bringing an air of mystery as well as a talent that could transform the bar’s drinks. A 7 Million YouTuber arrives with the boundless charisma that has made performance and self-expression a way of life. A Sexy Slick Guy, strikingly attractive and confident in his body, adds another vivid presence to the group. Joining them is the Guard, a dependable protector who watches over the women visiting Lolo BAR.

Surrounded by these distinctive new companions, Makgeolli decides to work with them. What had been an uncertain, frustrating preparation becomes a charged countdown to the long-awaited opening day. With nervous anticipation, he welcomes the moment when Lolo BAR finally opens its doors. The guests and staff are invited to become pleasantly drunk, seductively drunk, and, above all, to raise their glasses together: CHEERS.

At its heart, the musical celebrates a second chance pursued through collective energy rather than individual pride. Lolo BAR becomes a place where old dreams, hidden skills, flamboyant personalities, protection, pleasure, and shared excitement meet in one exuberant toast.

OFFICIAL TEXT: 《1980년 중반. 전주의 팔달로에는 모락모락 따뜻한 연기가 아침의 시작을 알린다. 부지런하게 아침을 시작하는 마을 주민들이 하나 둘 모이기 시작한다. 주민들이 모여 있는 공터 주변으로 명진제빵소를 비롯한 많은 가게들이 자리 잡고 있다. 가게들 뒤편으로 커다랗게 자리를 지키고 있는 전동성당은 이곳이 아주 오래전부터 여러 사람들이 모여 있었다는 것을 알려준다. 아주 오랜 시간동안 빵 굽는 냄새로 이곳에 아침을 알렸던 김사장은 자신의 아들 명진이가 제빵소를 이어받는 것이 못마땅하다. 전주의 알아주는 기업이었던 백양에 충분히 들어갈 수 있는 똑똑한 아들이 자신과 같이 제빵사를 하는 것이 답답한 김사장이다. 마을사람들의 뱃속을 따뜻하고 든든하게 채워주는 88콩나물국밥집을 운영하는 현옥은 빵을 너무너무 좋아하는 사랑스러운 딸 방순이와 함께 지내고 있다. 여자둘이 살아가기에 호락하지 않은 세상이지만 서로가 서로를 누구보다 의지하며 살아간다. 방순이는 고등학교를 졸업하고 현옥을 돕기 위해 학교에 진학하기보다는 테이프를 만드는 공장에 취업을 선택했다. 가수가 되고 싶다는 꿈을 포기하지 않고 언젠가 이 테이프에 자신의 노래가 담길 날을 꿈꾸며 노래 만드는 일을 계속해 나아간다. 그 시절 우리는 소박하지만 따뜻한 동네에 살았다. 그 누구에게나 마음의 어려움이 있었음에도 불구하고 말이다. 그렇기에 그 시절 우리에게 필요했던건 한 입 가득 입안을 채워 줄, 또 마음을 채워 줄 따뜻하고 달콤한 위로이지 않았을까? 1980년대 어느 날, 오늘도 팔달로의 한 빵 가게에서는 달콤한 위로가 필요한 이웃들을 위해 아침마다 빵 굽는 냄새가 맛있게 퍼진다.》 OFFICIAL CHARACTER LIST: 《김사장(제빵소 사장) / 명진(김사장的兒子,要接手麵包店) / 현옥(88 콩나물국밥집 老闆娘) / 방순(현옥的女兒,想當歌手,在錄音帶工廠上班) + 群戲》
synopsis:
Warm steam rises at daybreak along Paldal-ro in mid-1980s Jeonju, drawing early-rising residents toward the open space among the neighbourhood shops. Myeongjin Bakery stands at its centre, its familiar scent of fresh bread mingling with the activity of a community that has gathered here for generations beneath the watchful presence of Jeondong Cathedral. For a long time, Mr. Kim has announced each morning by baking bread, but he cannot welcome the prospect of his son Myeongjin inheriting the bakery. Intelligent enough to secure a position at Baegyang, one of Jeonju's respected companies, Myeongjin seems to his father destined for a more promising path than that of a baker. Yet the work of the bakery continues to anchor the neighbourhood, offering warmth and nourishment to those who pass through its doors.

Nearby, Hyeonok runs the 88 Bean Sprout Soup Rice Restaurant, feeding the village with bowls that are both warming and filling. She lives with her affectionate daughter Bangsun, who loves bread deeply. Life is not easy for the two women, but mother and daughter depend on one another more than anyone else. After graduating from high school, Bangsun chooses employment at a cassette-tape factory rather than continuing her education, hoping to help Hyeonok. She refuses, however, to abandon her dream of becoming a singer. As she makes tapes, she imagines a day when one will carry her own song.

Everyone on Paldal-ro carries private worries, even within a modest neighbourhood sustained by everyday kindness. Each morning, the bread oven opens again, sending out the delicious promise of a sweet consolation for neighbours whose stomachs and hearts both need to be filled.

The musical centres on ordinary people facing work, family expectations, economic hardship, and deferred dreams. Through bread, shared meals, music, and mutual reliance, it finds tenderness in the small rituals that help a community endure.

synopsis:
Its thirteen songs are all Korean hits of the 1970s and 80s, the title among them. At a nightclub, Hyeon-gu, a young man who dreams of music and freedom, meets Seon-hui, whose belief in him gives his ambitions a warmth and certainty he has not known before. She supports and encourages him as their affection deepens into love, becoming a steady presence while he pursues the future he has imagined. When Hyeon-gu's first album succeeds, it seems that the life he and Seon-hui have hoped for is finally beginning. Recognition arrives, opportunities multiply, and the spotlight that once represented possibility now shines directly upon him.

Yet success does not bring the uncomplicated happiness Hyeon-gu expects. As his career rises, the demands and allure of public attention gradually draw him away from Seon-hui. The distance between them creates conflict, forcing both of them to confront the damage caused by separation and the changing shape of their relationship. Although they struggle through this painful period, Hyeon-gu and Seon-hui eventually find their way back toward one another. Their renewed closeness suggests that the connection formed when he was still simply a young dreamer has endured the pressures of fame.

Their reconciliation is shadowed, however, by Seon-hui's failing health. As she loses her strength, Hyeon-gu carries her final wish in his heart, preserving it as something more lasting than the success that once seemed so important. After Seon-hui leaves, he must face an absence that music alone cannot immediately erase. In time, he turns again to the art that first brought their lives together, using music to endure his grief and to move beyond the weight of loss. Rather than remaining trapped in sorrow, Hyeon-gu gathers what Seon-hui gave him and steps forward into a new life.

The musical centres on youthful aspiration, love tested by fame, and the emotional cost of pursuing success. It also portrays music as both a vessel for memory and a means of surviving loss, allowing Hyeon-gu to transform grief into the courage to continue.

synopsis:
In 1984, at Machang Middle School, Misuk sings more brightly than anyone else, carrying the dream of becoming a singer. Her voice stops Gyeongho in his tracks. Captivated at first hearing, he gathers the courage to approach her, and an awkward yet tender first love begins between the two teenagers.

Their feelings grow through the ordinary days of school and the shared excitement of imagining the futures that lie ahead. Misuk keeps singing toward the life she wants, while Gyeongho remains close to her, moved by both her voice and her determination. Rather than standing in the way of each other's ambitions, they encourage one another, finding happiness in the hopes they hold together.

Around them are Junhui, Gwangsu, Juwon, Seonhui, Sowon, and Harin, who inhabit the world of the young couple as Misuk and Gyeongho pass through a time of bright songs, tentative courage, and first affection. For Misuk, singing is more than a youthful pastime: it is the dream that gives her life direction. For Gyeongho, the girl whose voice first drew him near becomes someone he wants to cherish and support.

Yet just as their days seem filled with promise, Misuk suffers an unexpected accident. The sudden event interrupts the happiness they have shared and leaves their future uncertain, placing both their love and their dreams before an unforeseen turning point.

At its heart, the musical celebrates youthful dreams, the emotional power of song, and the fragile sweetness of first love. It also asks how a promise of lasting devotion can endure when an unforeseen accident changes the course of two young lives.

OFFICIAL TEXT: 《작품에 관하여 피할 수 없는 이별의 순간, 누군가는 붙잡고, 누군가는 도망치고, 누군가는 괜찮은 척 살아갑니다. 이별을 마주할 용기가 없는 사람들을 위한 이별대행사 'EXIT'. 이별을 대신 전하고 그 이별통보를 받는 사람들. <충분한 이별>은 사람은 어떻게 타인과 헤어지고, 어떻게 상처를 받아들이며, 어떻게 그 상처를 안고 다시 살아갈 수 있는가를 이야기하는 작품입니다. 연인과의 이별, 가족과의 이별, 과거의 상처와의 이별, 죄책감과 미련과의 이별 — 이 작품이 말하고 싶은 것은 '이별'이 아니라…》 OFFICIAL CHARACTER LIST: 《최현빈(1989년 4월생, 배우 김윤·이명훈? ) / 박성훈(1989년 12월생) / 강혜진(1990년 3월생) / 차민지(1992년 5월생) / 최소민(1992년 10월생) / 최준석(1980년 11월생) —— 官方人物介紹逐一附出生年月》
synopsis:
At EXIT, an agency that delivers breakups on behalf of people too frightened to face them, farewells arrive in many forms. Some clients cannot bring themselves to let go; others run from the moment of parting, while still others carry on as if nothing has happened. EXIT steps into the space between those who choose to end a relationship and those left to receive the news, becoming a messenger for words that their owners cannot say themselves.

Around the agency, separation is never limited to one kind of loss. A lover may be gone, but so may a family member, a former self, or the possibility of undoing an old wound. Hyunbin Choi, Seonghun Park, Hyejin Kang, Minji Cha, Somin Choi, and Junseok Choi each stand near such thresholds, linked by the difficult work of confronting what has been left unsaid. Their stories move through the aftermath of endings: the shock of being told goodbye, the urge to cling to someone already departing, the impulse to disappear before one can be hurt, and the exhausting performance of pretending to be all right.

As EXIT delivers parting messages, the people involved must reckon with wounds that cannot simply be handed over to another person. The losses they face include not only relationships with lovers and family, but also ties to guilt, lingering attachment, and pain inherited from the past. A breakup may be announced by a stranger, yet the act of accepting it remains intensely personal. Each farewell asks whether a person can acknowledge hurt rather than evade it, and whether life can continue while carrying scars that may never wholly vanish.

Ultimately, the musical considers how people part from others, receive pain, and learn to live again with it. Its concern is not simply farewell itself, but the courage required to face it.

synopsis:
In the corner of a dressing room, at the centre of an empty stage, and somewhere inside a theatre deserted by everyone else, an unseen presence is tended at the same hour every day. Three actors remain in the ageing building: Eunha, Albar, Jaegyeong, and Duri. Unable to leave for reasons of their own, they endure life in a cramped space behind the stage, holding on as the theatre around them slowly loses its breath. Once each performance ends and the audience has gone, their real work begins.

Their nights are interrupted by phones that never stop ringing, messages they cannot read, and calls that go unanswered. They escape onto the stage as though running from their private burdens, yet fewer and fewer people come to watch. The theatre grows quieter, its fading life mirrored in the loneliness each of them carries. Eunha wonders whether waiting for a dead signal can still be love. Albar urges someone not to feel alone, insisting that the one beside them is not Albar but themselves. Jaegyeong admits that it was not all right, and that perhaps this, too, can be all right. Duri resolves to make others laugh before anyone can discover the real self hidden beneath the performance.

Then, one day, an unidentified sound rises from the dressing room. What has always been there vanishes. In the darkness that follows, unease spreads through the theatre, and the fragile routine binding its remaining inhabitants begins to shift. On a night where loneliness and fear cross paths, a story that begins with laughter gradually opens into quiet feeling and lingering emotion. At last, the real show begins.

At its heart, the musical is about the encounters that alter a life, even when they arrive unexpectedly in a place that seems to be fading away. It brings loneliness, fear, performance, and human connection together, suggesting that facing what is absent may reveal what has been beside us all along.
